findings.failure_path: Delete a genuine security or workflow obligation from a regular 100644 owner Markdown file, add no lines, and make the owner's sole ledger row source-refuted with observed-failure:no, any URL, and a pointer such as `README.md#a`. If README contains the letter `a`, `body.include?(anchor)` accepts it although it identifies no obligation map. The structural deletion predicate passes and all_rows_source_refuted lifts the RED floor, producing a false green for unaccounted data loss. Case H tests only a nonexistent anchor, so it misses this cheap existing-substring bypass.
findings.smallest_fix: Require a zero-loss pointer to resolve to a proper heading or an explicitly structured obligation-map entry, remove the unrestricted `body.include?(anchor)` fallback, and add regressions for one-character and unrelated-existing-substring pointers; until the pointer is bound to the withdrawn obligation, do not let source-refuted lift the owner RED floor.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Symlink, submodule, mode-change, non-Markdown, binary-numstat, and added-line shapes fail closed, but the zero-loss check remains cheaply satisfiable: any substring in any repository file counts as an anchor. No regression covers this or cross-round containment.

Containment fails because an arbitrary pure deletion of real obligations can self-clear with any URL and a one-character pointer into an unrelated file; the sole-row source-refuted exemption then lifts the owner RED floor without proving zero loss.
